clue.text: Kit he's left out for poacher?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the phrase are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gamekeeper's equipment has been left out ready for a poacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poacher' tempts as a person stealing game; here it is a cooking vessel, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lidded pan used to cook whole fish gently in liquid, so it is a kitchen utensil for poaching.

clue.text: Nothing at all on sides of carriage clock

indicators.note: on in a down clue means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: FA is short for sweet Fanny Adams, British slang for nothing at all

indicators.note: the sides of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of carriage

explanation.surface: Nothing at all is on either side of a carriage clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweet FA (Fanny Adams) is British slang for nothing; a carriage clock is a small portable clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Clock is slang for a person's face, and also a clock's dial is its face.

clue.text: Lion maybe intermittently sick with harmful fighting

indicators.note: intermittently means every other letter is taken

parts.note: alternate letters of sick

indicators.note: fighting suggests the letters scrap and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: A lion, perhaps, feeling poorly after a nasty fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lion is a player for the British and Irish Lions rugby team, so one could be this position.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rugby position, the player feeding the scrum, and a Lion is a touring rugby international.

clue.text: Decking man secures base of patio

indicators.note: secures means holds within itself

parts.note: a king is a piece, or man, in chess

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of a word is its last letter

parts.note: last letter of patio

explanation.surface: A man laying decking fixes the bottom of a patio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decking' sounds like garden timber but means knocking down; KO is a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: Koing is knocking out, flooring an opponent, just as decking someone means punching them down.

clue.text: Criminal, say, that's disgusting; one blocking kick

indicators.note: blocking means sitting inside and obstructing the other word

parts.note: to toe a ball is to kick it
ugh is the exclamation of disgust
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A villain, disgusted, has one obstructing kick.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also names the puzzle series itself; a toughie is a tough guy, such as a hoodlum.
explanation.definitionFit: A toughie is a hard, aggressive person, of which a hoodlum is one example.

clue.text: Tales about drink wherein not a little is a lot?

definitions.text: wherein not a little is a lot?

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: lies are tall tales
a tot is a small drink

explanation.surface: Stories over a drink in which understatement means plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: This figure of speech is understatement by negating the opposite, as in 'not bad' meaning good.

clue.text: Promise Germany conflict is over

indicators.note: over signals turning the pieces over, so they are read backwards

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
a row is a quarrel or conflict

explanation.surface: A pledge from Berlin that the fighting has ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To give your word is to give a solemn pledge or assurance.

clue.text: Best old Morecambe and Wise perhaps returning — about time

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters go around the next one
returning means the pieces come back, read in reverse

parts.note: Morecambe and Wise were a famous British comedy pair, an example of a duo

explanation.surface: The best of the old comic double act is coming back, about time too.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British TV comedy double act. 'Best' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to beat or surpass them.

clue.text: Shocked bird scoffing mass unexpectedly burst

indicators.note: scoffing means eating, so the bird takes the other letters inside

parts.note: a duck is a bird
M is the symbol for mass

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters arrive in a surprising order

explanation.surface: A startled bird gobbles a lot, then suddenly bursts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbstruck means so astonished as to be speechless.

clue.text: Ponder when half-cut about beginning to ring a best friend

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes around the letter
half-cut tells us to cut the word in half, keeping only its first four letters

parts.note: to cogitate is to ponder

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of ring

explanation.surface: Someone thinking, a little drunk, about phoning a close pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' reads as tipsy but tells you to halve COGITATE to COGI; 'about' then wraps COGI around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is called man's best friend, and the corgi is a breed of small dog.

clue.text: Final 6 translated mit umlaut

definitions.note: 6 refers to the answer at 6 across, a word; a final word is a last demand

indicators.note: translated suggests turning German into something else, so the letters are converted into a new order

explanation.surface: German words with an umlaut being rendered into English.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference 6 is WORD, so the definition reads 'final word'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultimatum is a last demand, beyond which no further negotiation is possible.

clue.text: Bloke making claim he falsified

indicators.note: falsified means the letters are faked into a different order

explanation.surface: A man making a claim that he faked.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is a typical man's name, so it stands for any chap.

clue.text: Rob, exhausted, still pursuing capture?

parts.note: to mug is to rob in the street
shot is slang for worn out, exhausted

explanation.surface: A worn-out robber still chasing a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is a photo, and 'capture' is an arrest: the photo follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A police photograph of a suspect's face is taken after arrest, so it is a picture following an arrest.

clue.text: Stand in the way of punch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to thwart or oppose
second meaning: a boxing blow thrown across the opponent's lead

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for opposing someone's plans and a noun for a type of boxing blow.

clue.text: Bishop possibly utilising one for whom rose could be pink

definitions.text: one for whom rose could be pink

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: possibly means the word utilising might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A bishop employing someone who sees roses as pink.
explanation.walkthrough: Rose is the French word for pink, so someone who speaks two languages could read 'rose' as a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A person fluent in two languages would know rose is the French word for pink.

clue.text: Title insurance, but not contents, covering house on front

indicators.note: covering means the outer letters wrap around the rest
without its contents a word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of insurance

indicators.note: on means house is placed after front

parts.note: the van is the front of an army

explanation.surface: Title insurance on a house, as in a property deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' belongs to the insurance phrase in the surface but is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the name of Walter Scott's novel, a book title.

clue.text: Pagan wants warm layer

parts.note: to heat is to warm
a hen is an egg layer

explanation.surface: A pagan needs a warm jumper or extra layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like clothing but is something that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen is someone who does not follow a major religion, an unbeliever.

clue.text: Fish head from smoked kipper

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of smoked
one who kips, or naps, is a napper

explanation.surface: A fish head taken from a smoked herring.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper here is a sleeper, from kip, a nap; NAPPER is also slang for the head, a neat red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The red snapper is a common food fish of warm seas.

clue.text: Element of autism so upsetting after onset of paranoia

indicators.note: after means the anagram follows this letter
the onset of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of paranoia

indicators.note: upsetting means the letters are overturned and rearranged

explanation.surface: A factor in autism made upsetting by a start of paranoia.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium is a chemical element, the metal with symbol K.

clue.text: Exaggerate through inversion of Eb

parts.note: in can mean by way of or through
Eb is musical notation for E flat; inverting the order of its two words gives flat E

explanation.surface: A musical instruction to overstate by inverting E flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflate a figure is to exaggerate or overstate it.

clue.text: Ban qualification held by climbing fiend

indicators.note: held by means placed inside the other word
climbing in a down clue means read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: an ogre is a monstrous fiend
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration degree

explanation.surface: A ban on a qualification held by a monstrous climber.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, especially on trade with a country.

clue.text: Prudent independent cut back most of credit

indicators.note: back means the two pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to lop is to cut

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: on tick means on credit

explanation.surface: A sensible independent trader cutting back most of their borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic means shrewd and sensible, the wise course in the circumstances.

clue.text: Bewilders quietly with unintroduced gags

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, quietly

indicators.note: unintroduced means without its first letter

parts.note: muzzles are gags that silence

explanation.surface: Quietly telling jokes without setting them up confuses people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gags' looks like jokes but here means silencing devices.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle someone is to perplex or confuse them.

clue.text: Censure suppressed by extremely ghoulish plot

indicators.note: suppressed by means held down inside the other letters
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of ghoulish
a rap is a rebuke or censure

explanation.surface: Criticism held back from a very gruesome storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a story but is a verb or noun for drawing a chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a chart of plotted points, and to graph is to plot.

clue.text: Financial adviser limited by exchange laws

indicators.note: limited by means confined within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A financial adviser constrained by currency exchange rules.
explanation.walkthrough: An angel in finance is a backer of a play or business; here the wider sense of guardian guide makes 'adviser' fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a private investor backing a venture, a guardian figure guiding money.

clue.text: Barry's bored by drivers by front of repair shops

indicators.note: bored by means the name is drilled through by the other letters

parts.note: Baz is a short form of the name Barry, keeping the possessive S

indicators.note: by means beside, so the letter follows

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motorists' organisation

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of repair

explanation.surface: Barry is bored rigid by motorists beside the repair shops.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the UK's Automobile Association, a motoring organisation for drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bazaars are markets or collections of stalls and shops, especially in the Middle East.

clue.text: Impromptu atomic construct erected following loss of uranium

indicators.note: erected in a down clue means set upright, so read upwards
following loss of means the word goes on after dropping this letter

parts.note: to build is to construct
U is the chemical symbol for uranium
A stands for atomic, as in A-bomb

explanation.surface: A makeshift atomic device built without uranium.
explanation.definitionFit: An ad-lib remark is made up on the spot, unrehearsed.

clue.text: Fish that is missing tail

indicators.note: missing tail means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: id est is Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A fish without its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Ides is the plural of ide, a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Learner follows popular classes as a rule

indicators.note: follows means this letter comes after the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
genera are biological classes
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner keeps after popular courses, which is the usual way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means usually, for the most part, in most cases.

clue.text: Island possessed by fat landowner

indicators.note: possessed by means held within the other word

parts.note: lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: An island owned by a stout landowner.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is the Scottish term for the owner of a landed estate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the owner of a large estate is called by this title.

clue.text: Set point — we shall see, ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of each word is taken

parts.note: last letter of point
last letter of we
last letter of shall
last letter of see

explanation.surface: A tennis set point, and the outcome remains to be seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set point' looks like one tennis phrase; 'Set' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tele is a British informal word for a television set.

clue.text: Sticky fluid secretion outwardly portrays reaction to stress

parts.note: goo is sticky stuff
sebum is an oily skin secretion

indicators.note: outwardly means only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of portrays

explanation.surface: A gooey skin secretion seen as a sign of tension.
explanation.definitionFit: Small bumps on the skin are raised by fear, cold or excitement, a bodily response to shock.
